title: Notable recent mathematics papers — arXiv batch 2026-11-11
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart. This ordering is inferred from theorem claims, cross-listing, corroboration, and reproducibility signals; citation evidence is limited for these very recent papers, so the report is not a popularity ranking.

sections.title: The Supercritical Ten Martini Problem
sections.abstract: The authors prove that for every nonconstant real-analytic one-frequency Schrödinger operator, the part of the spectrum with positive Lyapunov exponent is a Cantor set, using a higher-dimensional extension of a Kotani–almost-reducibility strategy.
sections.claimed_result: The authors’ Theorem 1.1 says that for nonconstant real-analytic v and irrational frequency α, Σ(v,α) intersected with the closure of the positive-Lyapunov region is a Cantor set, when nonempty; the whole spectrum is Cantor if L(E)>0 throughout it.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: One-frequency Schrödinger operators on ℓ²(ℤ), with a nonconstant real-analytic potential and irrational frequency; the primary conclusion concerns the positive-Lyapunov part of the spectrum.
sections.unique_caveat: It is not an unconditional Cantor-spectrum theorem for all energies: zero-Lyapunov portions are outside the main conclusion, and the paper notes that subcritical examples can have spectral intervals.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv introduction identifies this as proving You’s supercritical Cantor-spectrum conjecture, and Theorem 1.1 states the exact spectral scope; Wolfram MathWorld independently summarizes the result.

sections.title: A counterexample to the Erdős--Mahler conjecture
sections.abstract: For every real τ ≥ 4, the author constructs a Cantor set of numbers with irrationality exponent τ and infinitely many regular continued-fraction convergents whose numerators and denominators are powers of 2 and 3, respectively.
sections.claimed_result: The author’s main theorem constructs, for each real τ ≥ 4, a Cantor set Kτ in (1,2) whose members have irrationality exponent τ and infinitely many convergents of the form 2ᵃ/3ᵇ, thereby contradicting the stated conjecture.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Regular continued fractions of irrational real numbers; the construction prescribes convergents with numerator a power of 2 and denominator a power of 3, and applies to finite exponents τ ≥ 4.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated construction covers τ ≥ 4; it does not settle whether analogous sets exist for every finite exponent below 4.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper claims a counterexample to a 1939 conjecture, gives a precise construction, and includes a Lean 4 formalization; Wolfram MathWorld now cites the claimed counterexample.

sections.title: The Proof of the Alon--Kim Conjecture
sections.abstract: For fixed integers k ≥ t ≥ 1 and ε > 0, the authors prove that every k-uniform multihypergraph whose distinct edges intersect in at most t vertices has edge-chromatic number at most (t−1+1/t+ε)Δ once its maximum degree Δ is sufficiently large.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim that for every fixed k,t,ε in the stated range there is a sufficiently large degree threshold above which the conjectured edge-coloring inequality holds for all such multihypergraphs.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite k-uniform multihypergraphs; any two distinct edges meet in at most t vertices; k,t and positive ε are fixed while Δ is sufficiently large.
sections.unique_caveat: This is asymptotic in maximum degree, not an exact bound for all finite degrees; the abstract does not give an explicit threshold in Δ.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a resolution of the Alon–Kim asymptotic edge-coloring conjecture with its quantifiers and bound, and identifies a combination of finite-dimensional convex optimization and probabilistic methods.

sections.title: The closure of the nonreal roots of bounded-height polynomials is connected exactly at pronic heights
sections.abstract: For the closure Cₕ of nonreal roots of integer polynomials with coefficient modulus at most h, the author proves that Cₕ is connected exactly when h=q(q−1) is pronic, and has at least five components otherwise.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims connectedness precisely at pronic heights 2, 6, 12, 20, …; at every other height there are at least five components, with further infinite-component results for specified height ranges.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Cₕ is the closure of the nonreal roots of integer polynomials whose coefficients have modulus at most the positive integer height h; the statement excludes nonzero real roots from the set being closed.
sections.unique_caveat: The general nonpronic conclusion gives a lower bound on the number of components, not an exact component count at every height; the abstract gives detailed infinite-component statements only for specified ranges and exceptions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper gives an exact if-and-only-if arithmetic classification, links complex-variable and number-theoretic settings, and the announcement lists a substantial Zenodo computational companion.

sections.title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus
sections.abstract: The author rules out a 13-vertex simplicial triangulation of the three-torus, narrowing its minimum vertex count to 14 or 15.
sections.claimed_result: The author’s Theorem 1.1 proves that no simplicial triangulation of T³ has 13 vertices; together with existing bounds and a 15-vertex construction, the minimum lies between 14 and 15.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite simplicial triangulations of the three-torus; the obstruction uses the g₂ lower bound and properties of fundamental groups of small simplicial complexes.
sections.unique_caveat: The result does not decide whether a 14-vertex triangulation exists, so it does not yet establish that the known 15-vertex triangulation is vertex-minimal.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: This excludes the first case left unresolved by the standard lower bound, using a g₂ inequality, fundamental-group analysis, and Alexander duality; Wolfram MathWorld independently notes the result and its consequence for the minimum.

sections.title: On the stable birational type of Fano threefolds
sections.abstract: For a very general cubic threefold X, the author claims that every smooth cubic threefold stably birational to X is isomorphic to X, and says the method also applies to a sextic double solid and a quartic threefold.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims stable birational rigidity within the smooth cubic threefolds for a very general cubic, with analogous applications to the named Fano threefolds and discussion of higher dimensions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The reference cubic is very general; the comparison is with smooth cubic threefolds stably birational to it. Other Fano cases and higher-dimensional questions are treated as applications or discussion.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated cubic result is for a very general reference variety, not every cubic threefold, and the abstract does not spell out the precise higher-dimensional conclusions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a rigidity result for stable birational equivalence and identifies applications to multiple Fano threefold families; the scope is concrete and theorem-like.

sections.title: The Q-gonality of X₁(42) is 12
sections.abstract: The author proves that both the 𝔽₅-gonality and ℚ-gonality of X₁(42) are 12, improving the previous lower bound of 10, and deduces the least degree supporting infinitely many rational points.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims gon_{𝔽₅}(X₁(42)) = gon_{ℚ}(X₁(42)) = 12; since J₁(42)(ℚ) is finite, 12 is the least degree in which X₁(42) has infinitely many rational points.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The modular curve is X₁(42); the claim concerns gonality over 𝔽₅ and ℚ, and uses finiteness of J₁(42)(ℚ) for the rational-point consequence.
sections.unique_caveat: The lower bound relies on an exhaustive Riemann–Roch computation and its reductions; the author records data for reproduction, but this report has not independently rerun the computation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper claims an exact invariant, improves a published lower bound, and reports a reproducible lower-bound computation over 743,231 Riemann–Roch spaces; the abstract notes an earlier search using reductions from van Hoeij’s code with the same outcome.
